body: @josepharhar @jnjaeschke I noticed a couple more cases. Once some of my WebKit work lands I'll upload tests for this as well.

<details><summary>AI review</summary>

Reviewed at 1ea5c9b (with WebKit/WebKit#75502 at 58a45c8 and wpt#63153 at bd5ebb2). Lint passes. I compared the WebKit code by reading it; I didn't run any tests.

**Suggestions**

- `source:58731-58746`, `source:60801-60804`: when a `selectedcontent` and an `option` are inserted together, the spec still updates the `selectedcontent` twice. Example: `select.append(buttonContainingSelectedcontent, new Option("one"))` on an empty, connected `select`. The option's insertion steps set *pending `selectedcontent` update*. Then the `selectedcontent` post-connection steps clone "one", and the option post-connection steps see the flag still set and clone it again, which produces 2 mutation records. As far as I can tell WebKit produces 1: `updateSelectedContent(HTMLSelectedContentElement&)` records `m_selectedContentOption`, and the option's `updateSelectedContentIfSelectedOptionChanged()` then does nothing. This was already double before the PR, but it's the "updated too much" case the PR is about, and wpt#63153 doesn't test it. Either have the `selectedcontent` post-connection steps return when its *cached `select`*'s pending update is true (the option post-connection steps or the microtask will cover it), or confirm the double update is OK and add a test whose result both sides agree on.

**How the WebKit PR compares**

Most of it lines up with the spec PR:
- The `select` pending flag works the same way: the update clears it, and the microtask does nothing once it's cleared.
- The `selectedcontent` pending update and moving steps are a line-by-line match, including the `wasDisabled`/`oldSelect` early return and finding the `select` when the microtask runs.
- The new `selectedcontent` removing steps recalculate disabledness, as in the spec.
- When a `select` that already contains options is inserted, the options' post-connection steps are skipped because their owner `select` didn't change (`ownerSelectChanged`). That corresponds to the spec's « » plus the pending flag being false.

There are two differences in mechanism:
- **Option post-connection.** WebKit tracks which option it last cloned into the `selectedcontent` elements (`m_selectedContentOption`) and updates only if the selected option changed. The spec has no such state and relies on the pending flag. That difference causes the Suggestion above.
- **Removing or moving an option.** WebKit queues an update if the option is selected or nothing has been cloned yet. The spec queues if the option is selected or the *selectedness setting algorithm* changed something. These can differ: in a list box (`size` > 1) with no selection, removing an unselected option makes WebKit queue an update that clears the `selectedcontent`, while the spec doesn't queue one. I think you'd only notice this if the `selectedcontent` has children that script added.

For the `selected` setter, WebKit already returns early when the value doesn't change, which matches the spec's new *hasChanged*. Setting `selected = false` on a dropdown's selected option, when it's also the first enabled one, re-clones it in both.

</details>
@zcorpan I applied the suggestions that made sense in the last commit here. I also made a tiny tweak based on a test @josepharhar had submitted to WPT.

Q1: a `selectedcontent` can still be updated twice in one insertion. The `option` post-connection steps update every `selectedcontent` and clear *pending `selectedcontent` update*. A `selectedcontent` inserted after the option then sees the flag false and updates itself again:

* `select.append(new Option("two", "two", true, true), divWithSelectedcontent)` when `select` already has a `selectedcontent`: the new one gets 2 mutation records.
* `select.options[0].remove(); select.append(new Option("three"), divWithSelectedcontent)`: also 2.

Should we:

* a. Keep as is: it needs a second `selectedcontent` or an update already pending.
* b. Have the `selectedcontent` insertion steps queue the update, and its post-connection steps run a pending update like the `option` ones do, so whichever runs first updates once.

<details><summary>Option b details</summary>

Proposed (not applied): [spec](https://github.com/zcorpan/html/commits/zcorpan/spec-review/html-13005/q1-b), [tests](https://github.com/zcorpan/wpt/commits/zcorpan/spec-review/html-13005/q1-b). It needs no new state. Inserting a `selectedcontent` while an update is pending then updates it synchronously, as inserting an `option` already does, which changes one expectation in `selectedcontent-queued-update.html`. It also updates the select's other `selectedcontent` elements, as moving one already does.

</details>
